account: SK Telecom and project partners developed CareVia, a vision AI that detects and summarizes behavior to support care planning for people with developmental disabilities. On 7 March 2025, Bizhankook described the deployment at a center in Dobong and quoted outside voices, without outcome data. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), with information current as of June 2025, SK Telecom reports that recording time fell from three hours to five minutes per session. It also reports 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents in a 2024 intervention study, which it describes as a clinical study with Severance Hospital. The ITU account cites a 2011 World Health Organization and World Bank report as the source of the 76.5% figure and lists no Severance Hospital publication. Its supplied reference therefore does not identify that study. The clinical result remains unverified, and the effect of the AI is not separated from the other elements of care. SK Telecom's later reports give different outcome figures. On 10 June 2026 it reported that recording time fell by up to 90% and that challenging behaviors fell by 34.6% after tailored intervention. Dealsite reported on 6 October 2026 that CareVia still ran at 12 sites, short of the company's target of 18 sites by the end of 2025. A company official linked the shortfall to budgets.

fields.headline: SK Telecom says *CareVia* cut recording work and self-harm in care
fields.title: AI-Powered Behavior Recognition for Developmental Disability

provenance.basis: SHA-256 of the public case, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public case and its assessments

fields.account: SK Telecom and project partners developed CareVia, a vision AI that detects and summarizes behavior to support care planning for people with developmental disabilities. On 7 March 2025, Bizhankook described the deployment at a center in Dobong and quoted outside voices, without outcome data. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), with information current as of June 2025, SK Telecom reports that recording time fell from three hours to five minutes per session. It also reports 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents in a 2024 intervention study, which it describes as a clinical study with Severance Hospital. The ITU account cites a 2011 World Health Organization and World Bank report as the source of the 76.5% figure and lists no Severance Hospital publication. Its supplied reference therefore does not identify that study. The clinical result remains unverified, and the effect of the AI is not separated from the other elements of care. SK Telecom's later reports give different outcome figures. On 10 June 2026 it reported that recording time fell by up to 90% and that challenging behaviors fell by 34.6% after tailored intervention. Dealsite reported on 6 October 2026 that CareVia still ran at 12 sites, short of the company's target of 18 sites by the end of 2025. A company official linked the shortfall to budgets.

purpose: Help care teams identify and respond to challenging behaviors.

ratings.reason: SK Telecom reports that behavior-recording work fell from about three hours to five minutes per session. In June 2026 it reported that recording time fell by up to 90%.

SK Telecom reports 76.5% fewer self-harm incidents in a 2024 intervention study, and its supplied reference does not identify that study. In June 2026 it reported that challenging behaviors fell by 34.6% after tailored intervention. No independent source confirms either figure, and the separate effect of the AI is unknown. No source reports injury severity or how long the improvement lasted.
